meta.series: DSA for Freshers: Mid-level Company Roadmap
meta.level_title: Foundation: Arrays, Matrix, Strings, Bits, Math, Recursion
meta.note: company_tags indicative hain (frequently asked trends), official guarantee nahi.

theory.concept: Matrix ek array of arrays hai: a[i][j] me i row aur j column hota hai. C++ me data row-major store hota hai, isliye row-wise traversal cache-friendly hota hai.
key_points: Traversal O(m*n); in-place problems me extra matrix banane se space O(m*n) lagti hai
Transpose: a[i][j] <-> a[j][i] sirf j > i ke liye swap (dobara swap karoge to wapas original)
90 degree clockwise rotation = transpose + har row reverse
Spiral/boundary traversal: top, bottom, left, right 4 boundaries shrink karte jao
Direction arrays dr[] = {0,1,0,-1}, dc[] = {1,0,-1,0} se right/down/left/up handle hota hai
pitfalls: Non-square matrix me in-place transpose nahi hota
Spiral me single row/column edge case (boundary check dobara karo)
m aur n ko ulta likh dena

theory.concept: Numbers ko binary bits ki tarah treat karke operations karna: &, |, ^, ~, <<, >>. Ye constant-time aur memory-efficient tricks deta hai.
key_points: n & 1 => last bit (odd/even check)
n & (n-1) => lowest set bit hata deta hai (Brian Kernighan); set bits count O(set bits)
Power of two: n > 0 && (n & (n-1)) == 0
x ^ y me wahi bits 1 hote hain jahan x aur y alag hain (Hamming distance)
Left shift by k = multiply by 2^k, right shift by k = divide by 2^k
Bit problems me unsigned (uint32_t) use karo taaki sign-extension ka confusion na ho
pitfalls: Operator precedence: n & 1 == 0 galat hai, (n & 1) == 0 likho
1 << 31 signed int me overflow hai, 1u ya 1LL use karo
Negative numbers ka right shift implementation-defined hota hai

theory.concept: Jab array me end me extra jagah ho (ya shifting costly ho) to peeche se fill karo. Isse unprocessed elements overwrite nahi hote.
key_points: Merge sorted arrays in-place: i = m-1, j = n-1, k = m+n-1 pointers
Carry-based problems (Plus One, Add Binary) right-to-left chalte hain
Jab naya element sabse bada ya sabse chhota decide ho jaye, usse final jagah par rakh do
pitfalls: Pehle se start karoge to elements overwrite honge
Loop condition me j >= 0 hi kaafi hota hai (i bacha ho to wo already sahi jagah par hai)

theory.concept: Naive matching har position par try karta hai (O(n*m)). KMP prefix function (LPS) se mismatch par pattern me wapas kahan jaana hai pehle se pata hota hai, isliye O(n+m).
key_points: LPS[i] = pattern[0..i] ka longest proper prefix jo suffix bhi hai
Mismatch par k = lps[k-1], text pointer peeche nahi jata
Rotation check: s ka rotation hamesha s+s ka substring hota hai
Subsequence (order preserve, contiguous nahi) ka check two pointers se O(n)
pitfalls: std::string::find ka worst case library par depend karta hai

theory.concept: Agar sequence repeat hone lagti hai to slow (1 step) aur fast (2 step) pointer kisi point par mil jaate hain. Extra set ki zaroorat nahi, O(1) space.
key_points: Happy Number me next(n) = digit squares ka sum; ya to 1 aata hai ya cycle
HashSet approach: seen set me store karo, repeat mila to cycle
Floyd approach: slow = next(slow), fast = next(next(fast)), mile to cycle
Same idea linked list cycle (Level 3) me aayegi
pitfalls: Termination condition (1 par ruk jao) bhoolna
Cycle ka length/start alag cheez hai

theory.concept: Kayi recursion problems ek recurrence deti hain (Hanoi: T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1; Josephus: J(n) = (J(n-1) + k) % n). Recurrence ko loop me convert ya closed form me badal kar exponential se polynomial/constant time aata hai.
key_points: Recurrence likho -> base case likho -> complexity nikalo
Climbing Stairs: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), Fibonacci jaisa; O(1) space me roll karo
Hanoi minimum moves = 2^n - 1 (induction se prove hota hai)
Top-down recursion + memo = bottom-up DP (Level 5)
pitfalls: Bina memo ke overlapping subproblems par recursion
Hanoi brute n > 30 par practically slow

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.problem_statement: Given daily prices, buy on one day and sell on a later day to maximize profit. Return the max profit (0 if no profit possible).
problems.description: Sell hamesha buy ke baad hona chahiye. Sirf ek transaction allowed hai.
problems.theory: Har din ke liye ab tak ka minimum price yaad rakho aur dekho aaj bechne par kitna profit hota.

brute_force.approach: Har (i, j) pair ke liye prices[j] - prices[i] nikalo.
brute_force.code_cpp: int maxProfit(const vector<int>& p){ int best = 0, n = p.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) best = max(best, p[j] - p[i]); return best; }

optimized.approach: Ek pass: minPrice update karo, best = max(best, price - minPrice).
optimized.code_cpp: int maxProfit(const vector<int>& p){ int mn = INT_MAX, best = 0; for(int x : p){ mn = min(mn, x); best = max(best, x - mn); } return best; }

problems.explanation: Brute me har buy day ke liye saare future days dekhte hain. Optimized me 'best buy day' ko ek variable me compress kar liya.

problems.title: Merge Sorted Array (In-place)
problems.problem_statement: a has m valid elements followed by n empty slots; b has n elements. Merge b into a so that a is sorted.
problems.description: Result a hi me chahiye. Dono arrays pehle se sorted hain.
problems.theory: Peeche se fill karo: bada element end me rakho. Isse a ke valid elements overwrite nahi hote.

brute_force.approach: b ko a ke end me copy karo aur poora sort kar do.
brute_force.code_cpp: void mergeArr(vector<int>& a, int m, vector<int>& b, int n){ for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) a[m + i] = b[i]; sort(a.begin(), a.begin() + m + n); }

optimized.approach: Teen pointers i = m-1, j = n-1, k = m+n-1; bada wala a[k] me daalo.
optimized.code_cpp: void mergeArr(vector<int>& a, int m, vector<int>& b, int n){ int i = m - 1, j = n - 1, k = m + n - 1; while(j >= 0){ if(i >= 0 && a[i] > b[j]) a[k--] = a[i--]; else a[k--] = b[j--]; } }

problems.explanation: Aage se merge karte to a ke elements overwrite ho jaate. Peeche khali jagah hai, isliye wahan se fill karna safe hai. Sort wala brute sorted hone ka fayda waste karta hai.
edge_cases: All of b smaller than a

problems.title: Plus One
problems.problem_statement: A large integer is given as a digit array (most significant digit first). Add one and return the resulting digit array.
problems.description: Number itna bada ho sakta hai ki int/long long me fit na ho, isliye digit-wise handle karo.
problems.theory: Right se chalo: digit < 9 ho to +1 karke return; warna 0 karke carry aage. Agar poore 9 the to front me 1 lagao.

brute_force.approach: Digits ko long long number me convert karo, +1 karo aur wapas digits me tod do (sirf ~18 digits tak chalega).
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> plusOne(vector<int> d){ long long n = 0; for(int x : d) n = n * 10 + x; n++; string s = to_string(n); vector<int> r; for(char c : s) r.push_back(c - '0'); return r; }

optimized.approach: Right se scan; early return jab digit 9 se kam mile; end me 1 insert.
optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> plusOne(vector<int> d){ for(int i = (int)d.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--){ if(d[i] < 9){ d[i]++; return d; } d[i] = 0; } d.insert(d.begin(), 1); return d; }

problems.explanation: Brute approach 100 digit input par overflow karega. Digit array problems me hamesha carry logic se kaam karo.

problems.title: Pascal's Triangle
problems.problem_statement: Given numRows, generate the first numRows rows of Pascal's triangle.
problems.description: Har element apne upar ke do elements ka sum hota hai; edges par 1.
problems.theory: Row r, column c ki value = C(r, c). Previous row se: row[c] = prev[c-1] + prev[c].

brute_force.approach: Har cell ko nCr formula se alag compute karo.
brute_force.code_cpp:
long long nCr(int n, int r){ long long x = 1; for(int i = 0; i < r; i++) x = x * (n - i) / (i + 1); return x; }
vector<vector<int>> pascal(int n){ vector<vector<int>> t; for(int r = 0; r < n; r++){ vector<int> row; for(int c = 0; c <= r; c++) row.push_back((int)nCr(r, c)); t.push_back(row); } return t; }

optimized.approach: Previous row se current row banao; pehla aur aakhri 1.
optimized.code_cpp: vector<vector<int>> pascal(int n){ vector<vector<int>> t; for(int r = 0; r < n; r++){ vector<int> row(r + 1, 1); for(int c = 1; c < r; c++) row[c] = t[r-1][c-1] + t[r-1][c]; t.push_back(row); } return t; }

problems.explanation: Optimized me har cell O(1) me banta hai (do values ka sum). Output size hi O(n^2) hai, isliye ye optimal hai.

problems.title: Transpose Matrix (Square, In-place)
problems.problem_statement: Transpose an n x n matrix in-place: element (i, j) goes to (j, i).
problems.description: Rows columns ban jaate hain aur columns rows. Square matrix me extra matrix ki zaroorat nahi.
problems.theory: Sirf upper triangle (j > i) ke elements swap karo. Poore matrix par swap karoge to do baar swap hoke wapas original ho jayega.

brute_force.approach: Naya matrix banao, t[j][i] = a[i][j], phir copy back.
brute_force.code_cpp: void transposeM(vector<vector<int>>& a){ int n = a.size(); vector<vector<int>> t(n, vector<int>(n)); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = 0; j < n; j++) t[j][i] = a[i][j]; a = t; }

optimized.approach: In-place swap a[i][j] <-> a[j][i] for j > i.
optimized.code_cpp: void transposeM(vector<vector<int>>& a){ int n = a.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) swap(a[i][j], a[j][i]); }

problems.explanation: Diagonal elements khud apni jagah par hote hain. Ye step Rotate Image ka first half hai.

problems.title: Rotate Image 90 Degrees Clockwise
problems.problem_statement: Rotate an n x n matrix by 90 degrees clockwise in-place.
problems.description: Naya matrix allocate karna allowed nahi (in-place).
problems.theory: Rotation = transpose + har row ko reverse. Anticlockwise ke liye: transpose + har column reverse (ya pehle rows reverse).

brute_force.approach: Naya matrix b banao, b[j][n-1-i] = a[i][j], phir a = b.
brute_force.code_cpp: void rotateImg(vector<vector<int>>& a){ int n = a.size(); auto b = a; for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = 0; j < n; j++) b[j][n-1-i] = a[i][j]; a = b; }

optimized.approach: Transpose in-place, phir har row reverse.
optimized.code_cpp: void rotateImg(vector<vector<int>>& a){ int n = a.size(); for(int i = 0; i < n; i++) for(int j = i + 1; j < n; j++) swap(a[i][j], a[j][i]); for(auto& row : a) reverse(row.begin(), row.end()); }

problems.explanation: Brute me mapping formula (i, j) -> (j, n-1-i) yaad rakhni padti hai. Optimized me do simple steps ka combination hai, yaad rakhna aur debug karna dono aasan.

problems.title: Spiral Matrix
problems.problem_statement: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order starting from the top-left corner.
problems.description: Right -> down -> left -> up ke order me ghoomna hai jab tak saare elements na aa jaayein.
problems.theory: Boundary shrinking: top, bottom, left, right. Ek layer khatam hone par boundary andar aati hai. Direction badalne se pehle boundary check zaroori.

brute_force.approach: Visited matrix + direction arrays; deewar ya visited cell milne par turn.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> spiral(const vector<vector<int>>& a){ int m = a.size(), n = a[0].size(); vector<vector<bool>> v(m, vector<bool>(n, false)); int dr[4] = {0, 1, 0, -1}, dc[4] = {1, 0, -1, 0}; int r = 0, c = 0, d = 0; vector<int> res; for(int k = 0; k < m * n; k++){ res.push_back(a[r][c]); v[r][c] = true; int nr = r + dr[d], nc = c + dc[d]; if(nr < 0 || nr >= m || nc < 0 || nc >= n || v[nr][nc]){ d = (d + 1) % 4; nr = r + dr[d]; nc = c + dc[d]; } r = nr; c = nc; } return res; }

optimized.approach: Four boundaries (t, b, l, r) se layer-by-layer traversal, visited array nahi.
optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> spiral(const vector<vector<int>>& a){ vector<int> r; int t = 0, b = a.size() - 1, l = 0, rt = a[0].size() - 1; while(t <= b && l <= rt){ for(int j = l; j <= rt; j++) r.push_back(a[t][j]); t++; for(int i = t; i <= b; i++) r.push_back(a[i][rt]); rt--; if(t <= b){ for(int j = rt; j >= l; j--) r.push_back(a[b][j]); b--; } if(l <= rt){ for(int i = b; i >= t; i--) r.push_back(a[i][l]); l++; } } return r; }

problems.explanation: Single row/column par duplicate traversal na ho, isliye bottom aur left pass se pehle boundary check lagaya hai.

problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
problems.problem_statement: Array of n integers in range [1, n]. Return all numbers in [1, n] that do not appear.
problems.description: Duplicates ho sakte hain, isliye kuch numbers missing honge. O(1) extra space ki koshish karo.
problems.theory: Value ko index ki tarah use karo: a[v-1] ko negative mark karo. End me jo index positive reh gaya, i+1 missing hai.

brute_force.approach: 1 se n tak har number ke liye array me linear search.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> disappeared(const vector<int>& a){ int n = a.size(); vector<int> r; for(int x = 1; x <= n; x++){ bool f = false; for(int v : a) if(v == x){ f = true; break; } if(!f) r.push_back(x); } return r; }

optimized.approach: Index marking: a[abs(x)-1] ko negative karo; phir positive wale indices collect karo (input modify hota hai).
optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> disappeared(vector<int>& a){ for(int x : a){ int i = abs(x) - 1; if(a[i] > 0) a[i] = -a[i]; } vector<int> r; for(int i = 0; i < (int)a.size(); i++) if(a[i] > 0) r.push_back(i + 1); return r; }

problems.explanation: Range [1, n] hone ki wajah se value ko index banaya ja sakta hai. Negative sign ek free 'visited' flag hai. abs() isliye kyunki element pehle hi negative ho sakta hai.

problems.title: Roman to Integer
problems.problem_statement: Convert a Roman numeral string to an integer.
problems.description: Normally bade se chhota order me values add hoti hain; IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM me chhota pehle aata hai aur subtract hota hai.
problems.theory: Agar current symbol ki value next symbol se chhoti hai to subtract karo, warna add karo.

brute_force.approach: Special pairs (CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV) pehle dhundkar hatao aur unki value add karo, phir baaki symbols add.
brute_force.code_cpp: int romanToInt(string s){ vector<pair<string,int>> sp = {{"CM",900},{"CD",400},{"XC",90},{"XL",40},{"IX",9},{"IV",4}}; int r = 0; for(auto& p : sp){ size_t pos; while((pos = s.find(p.first)) != string::npos){ r += p.second; s.erase(pos, 2); } } for(char c : s){ switch(c){ case 'I': r += 1; break; case 'V': r += 5; break; case 'X': r += 10; break; case 'L': r += 50; break; case 'C': r += 100; break; case 'D': r += 500; break; case 'M': r += 1000; break; } } return r; }

optimized.approach: Ek pass: v[s[i]] < v[s[i+1]] ho to subtract, warna add.
optimized.code_cpp: int romanToInt(const string& s){ unordered_map<char,int> v = {{'I',1},{'V',5},{'X',10},{'L',50},{'C',100},{'D',500},{'M',1000}}; int r = 0; for(int i = 0; i < (int)s.size(); i++){ if(i + 1 < (int)s.size() && v[s[i]] < v[s[i+1]]) r -= v[s[i]]; else r += v[s[i]]; } return r; }

problems.explanation: Subtraction rule ko seedha 'chhota symbol bade se pehle' ke rule me badal diya, isliye special cases ki list nahi chahiye.

problems.title: Length of Last Word
problems.problem_statement: Return the length of the last word in a string of words and spaces.
problems.description: Trailing spaces ho sakte hain. Word = non-space characters ka maximal substring.
problems.theory: Peeche se scan karo: pehle trailing spaces skip, phir characters count karo jab tak space na mile.

brute_force.approach: Stringstream se saare words nikalo aur last ki length return.
brute_force.code_cpp: int lastWord(const string& s){ stringstream ss(s); string w, last; while(ss >> w) last = w; return last.size(); }

optimized.approach: Right se skip spaces, phir count.
optimized.code_cpp: int lastWord(const string& s){ int i = (int)s.size() - 1; while(i >= 0 && s[i] == ' ') i--; int len = 0; while(i >= 0 && s[i] != ' '){ len++; i--; } return len; }

problems.explanation: Poori string split karna zaroori nahi; sirf last word chahiye, isliye peeche se kaam shuru karo.

problems.title: Rotate String
problems.problem_statement: Return true if goal can be obtained from s by some number of left shifts (rotations).
problems.description: Ek shift me s ka pehla character end me chala jata hai.
problems.theory: Har rotation s+s ka substring hota hai. Length same ho to (s+s).find(goal) check karo.

brute_force.approach: Har k (0..n-1) ke liye rotation banao aur goal se compare.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool rotateString(const string& s, const string& g){ if(s.size() != g.size()) return false; int n = s.size(); for(int k = 0; k < n; k++) if(s.substr(k) + s.substr(0, k) == g) return true; return false; }

optimized.approach: Length check, phir (s+s) me goal ka search.
optimized.time: O(n) with KMP, library find me typically fast
optimized.code_cpp: bool rotateString(const string& s, const string& g){ return s.size() == g.size() && (s + s).find(g) != string::npos; }

problems.explanation: s+s me saare rotations ek saath chhupe hote hain (abcdeabcde). Length check zaroori, warna 'ab' ke andar 'abab' ka part mil sakta hai.

problems.title: Find Index of First Occurrence (strStr)
problems.problem_statement: Return the first index where needle occurs in haystack, or -1.
problems.description: Substring search implement karna hai bina library function ke.
problems.theory: Naive me mismatch par poora wapas jaate hain. KMP me LPS table se pattern me sahi jagah par jump karte hain, text pointer kabhi peeche nahi jata.

brute_force.approach: Har start index par needle ke saath compare.
brute_force.code_cpp: int strStr(const string& h, const string& n){ int a = h.size(), b = n.size(); for(int i = 0; i + b <= a; i++){ int j = 0; while(j < b && h[i + j] == n[j]) j++; if(j == b) return i; } return -1; }

optimized.approach: KMP: needle ka LPS array banao, phir haystack me match karo.
optimized.code_cpp: int strStr(const string& h, const string& n){ int m = n.size(); if(m == 0) return 0; vector<int> lps(m, 0); for(int i = 1, k = 0; i < m; i++){ while(k > 0 && n[i] != n[k]) k = lps[k-1]; if(n[i] == n[k]) k++; lps[i] = k; } for(int i = 0, k = 0; i < (int)h.size(); i++){ while(k > 0 && h[i] != n[k]) k = lps[k-1]; if(h[i] == n[k]) k++; if(k == m) return i - m + 1; } return -1; }

problems.explanation: Interview me aksar naive solution kaafi hota hai; KMP follow-up me poochha jata hai. LPS ek baar banta hai (O(m)) aur search O(n).

problems.title: Add Binary
problems.problem_statement: Given two binary strings, return their sum as a binary string.
problems.description: Strings 1e4 length tak ho sakti hain, isliye integer me convert nahi kar sakte.
constraints: Only '0' and '1', no leading zeros except '0'
problems.theory: School addition: right se bit-by-bit jodo, carry rakho, end me result ko reverse karo.

brute_force.approach: Dono ko integer me convert (stoll base 2), add, phir binary string me wapas (sirf ~62 bits tak).
brute_force.code_cpp: string addBinary(string a, string b){ long long x = stoll(a, nullptr, 2), y = stoll(b, nullptr, 2), s = x + y; if(s == 0) return "0"; string r; while(s){ r += char('0' + (s & 1)); s >>= 1; } reverse(r.begin(), r.end()); return r; }

optimized.approach: Two pointers i, j from the right + carry; loop tab tak jab tak i, j ya carry bacha ho.
optimized.code_cpp: string addBinary(string a, string b){ string r; int i = (int)a.size() - 1, j = (int)b.size() - 1, c = 0; while(i >= 0 || j >= 0 || c){ int s = c; if(i >= 0) s += a[i--] - '0'; if(j >= 0) s += b[j--] - '0'; r += char('0' + (s & 1)); c = s >> 1; } reverse(r.begin(), r.end()); return r; }

problems.explanation: Brute out_of_range de dega badi strings par. Carry = s >> 1 aur digit = s & 1 (bit manipulation ka practical use).

problems.title: Is Subsequence
problems.problem_statement: Return true if s is a subsequence of t (characters in the same order, not necessarily contiguous).
problems.description: Subsequence me characters delete kar sakte hain par order change nahi hota.

test_cases.explanation: a, b, c order me mile

problems.theory: Two pointers: t par chalo; jab t[j] == s[i] ho to i++. End me i == |s| ho to true.

brute_force.approach: Recursion: match ho to dono aage, warna sirf t aage (har step par do choices).
brute_force.code_cpp:
bool rec(const string& s, const string& t, int i, int j){ if(i == (int)s.size()) return true; if(j == (int)t.size()) return false; if(s[i] == t[j] && rec(s, t, i + 1, j + 1)) return true; return rec(s, t, i, j + 1); }
bool isSub(const string& s, const string& t){ return rec(s, t, 0, 0); }

optimized.approach: Greedy two pointers, ek pass.
optimized.code_cpp: bool isSub(const string& s, const string& t){ size_t i = 0; for(char c : t) if(i < s.size() && s[i] == c) i++; return i == s.size(); }

problems.explanation: Greedy kaam karta hai kyunki s ke next character ka sabse pehla match lena hamesha safe hai (baad me match rakhne ka koi fayda nahi).

problems.title: Number of 1 Bits (Hamming Weight)
problems.problem_statement: Return the number of set bits (1s) in the binary representation of an unsigned 32-bit integer.
problems.description: Set bits ginne hain, leading zeros ignore.
problems.theory: n & (n-1) lowest set bit ko 0 kar deta hai. Jitni baar ye operation ho, utne set bits.

brute_force.approach: Saare 32 bits check karo: (n >> i) & 1.
brute_force.code_cpp: int hammingWeight(uint32_t n){ int c = 0; for(int i = 0; i < 32; i++) if((n >> i) & 1) c++; return c; }

optimized.approach: Brian Kernighan: while(n) { n &= n - 1; c++; }
optimized.code_cpp: int hammingWeight(uint32_t n){ int c = 0; while(n){ n &= n - 1; c++; } return c; }

problems.explanation: Kernighan me loop sirf set bits ki sankhya jitni baar chalta hai. Built-in: __builtin_popcount(n) (GCC/Clang).

problems.title: Power of Two
problems.problem_statement: Return true if n is a power of two.
problems.description: n = 2^k for some k >= 0.
problems.theory: Power of two me exactly ek set bit hota hai. n & (n-1) wo bit hata deta hai, to result 0 hona chahiye (n > 0 ke saath).

brute_force.approach: n ko baar baar 2 se divide karo jab tak divisible ho; end me 1 bacha to true.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool isPow2(int n){ if(n <= 0) return false; while(n % 2 == 0) n /= 2; return n == 1; }

optimized.code_cpp: bool isPow2(int n){ return n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0; }

problems.explanation: Negative numbers aur 0 ko alag handle karna zaroori (n > 0). Bracket important hai: n & (n-1) ko == 0 se pehle bracket me rakho.

problems.title: Counting Bits (0 to n)
problems.problem_statement: For every i in [0, n], return the number of 1 bits in i as an array.
problems.description: Har number ke set bits alag-alag chahiye.
problems.theory: DP relation: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1). i ko ek position right shift karo to chhota number milta hai, jiska answer pehle se pata hai.

brute_force.approach: Har i ke liye bits ek-ek karke ginno.
brute_force.code_cpp: vector<int> countBits(int n){ vector<int> r(n + 1); for(int i = 0; i <= n; i++){ int c = 0, x = i; while(x){ c += x & 1; x >>= 1; } r[i] = c; } return r; }

optimized.code_cpp: vector<int> countBits(int n){ vector<int> r(n + 1, 0); for(int i = 1; i <= n; i++) r[i] = r[i >> 1] + (i & 1); return r; }

problems.explanation: Pichhle answers reuse karna DP ka core idea hai. Alternative: r[i] = r[i & (i-1)] + 1.

problems.title: Reverse Bits (32-bit)
problems.problem_statement: Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer.
problems.description: Bit position 0 position 31 par chali jati hai, 1 par 30, aur aise hi.
problems.theory: result ko left shift karke n ka last bit append karo, phir n ko right shift. 32 baar repeat.

brute_force.approach: Bits ko string me nikalo aur reverse order me wapas number banao.
brute_force.code_cpp: uint32_t reverseBits(uint32_t n){ string b; for(int i = 0; i < 32; i++) b += char('0' + ((n >> i) & 1)); uint32_t r = 0; for(char c : b) r = (r << 1) | (c - '0'); return r; }

optimized.approach: Direct bit shifting, no string.
optimized.code_cpp: uint32_t reverseBits(uint32_t n){ uint32_t r = 0; for(int i = 0; i < 32; i++){ r = (r << 1) | (n & 1); n >>= 1; } return r; }

problems.explanation: Dono O(1) hain kyunki size fixed 32 hai; fark extra memory aur constant factor me hai. Follow-up: mask-swap (16, 8, 4, 2, 1 bit blocks) se 5 steps me ho jata hai.

problems.title: Hamming Distance
problems.problem_statement: Return the number of bit positions where two integers differ.
problems.description: Dono numbers ke binary me kitni jagah bits alag hain.
problems.theory: x ^ y me 1 wahi hote hain jahan bits alag hain. Us result ke set bits count karo.

brute_force.approach: Har bit position par x aur y ke bits compare karo.
brute_force.code_cpp: int hammingDist(int x, int y){ int c = 0; for(int i = 0; i < 31; i++) if(((x >> i) & 1) != ((y >> i) & 1)) c++; return c; }

optimized.approach: c = popcount(x ^ y) using n &= n - 1.
optimized.code_cpp: int hammingDist(int x, int y){ int n = x ^ y, c = 0; while(n){ n &= n - 1; c++; } return c; }

problems.explanation: XOR 'difference detector' hai. Ye pichhle problem (Number of 1 Bits) ka direct reuse hai.

problems.title: Palindrome Number (Without String)
problems.problem_statement: Return true if integer x is a palindrome. Try without converting to string.
problems.description: Negative numbers palindrome nahi hote (minus sign).
problems.theory: Sirf aadhe digits reverse karo. Jab reversed half >= remaining first half ho jaye to compare karo. Isse overflow bhi nahi hota.

brute_force.approach: to_string karke reverse se compare.
brute_force.code_cpp: bool isPal(int x){ if(x < 0) return false; string s = to_string(x); string r(s.rbegin(), s.rend()); return s == r; }

optimized.approach: Last digit pop karke reversed half banao, loop jab tak x > r.
optimized.code_cpp: bool isPal(int x){ if(x < 0 || (x % 10 == 0 && x != 0)) return false; int r = 0; while(x > r){ r = r * 10 + x % 10; x /= 10; } return x == r || x == r / 10; }

problems.explanation: x == r/10 odd length handle karta hai (beech ka digit ignore). Trailing zero wale (10, 100) kabhi palindrome nahi, 0 ke alawa.

problems.title: Happy Number
problems.problem_statement: A number is happy if repeatedly replacing it by the sum of squares of its digits reaches 1. Return true if n is happy.
problems.description: Ya to 1 aayega ya koi cycle ban jayegi (kabhi 1 nahi aayega).
problems.theory: Sequence ka cycle detect karna hai: HashSet ya Floyd slow/fast pointers.

brute_force.approach: HashSet me seen numbers rakho; repeat mila to cycle.
brute_force.time: O(log n) per step, bounded steps
brute_force.code_cpp:
int sq(int n){ int s = 0; while(n){ int d = n % 10; s += d * d; n /= 10; } return s; }
bool isHappy(int n){ unordered_set<int> seen; while(n != 1 && !seen.count(n)){ seen.insert(n); n = sq(n); } return n == 1; }

optimized.approach: Floyd cycle detection: slow ek step, fast do step.
optimized.code_cpp:
int sq(int n){ int s = 0; while(n){ int d = n % 10; s += d * d; n /= 10; } return s; }
bool isHappy(int n){ int s = n, f = sq(n); while(f != 1 && s != f){ s = sq(s); f = sq(sq(f)); } return f == 1; }

problems.explanation: Digits square sum jaldi chhota ho jata hai (32-bit number ke liye max ~810), isliye sequence bounded hai aur cycle pakka banegi ya 1 aayega.

problems.title: Add Digits (Digital Root)
problems.problem_statement: Repeatedly add all digits of num until the result has one digit; return it.
problems.description: O(1) time aur bina loop/recursion ke solve karne ka follow-up poochha jata hai.
problems.theory: Digital root formula: num == 0 ? 0 : 1 + (num - 1) % 9. Reason: 10 ≡ 1 (mod 9), to number aur uske digits ka sum mod 9 me same hote hain.

brute_force.approach: Jab tak num >= 10, digits ka sum nikalte raho.
brute_force.code_cpp: int addDigits(int n){ while(n >= 10){ int s = 0; while(n){ s += n % 10; n /= 10; } n = s; } return n; }

optimized.approach: Closed-form formula.
optimized.code_cpp: int addDigits(int n){ return n == 0 ? 0 : 1 + (n - 1) % 9; }

problems.explanation: 9 ke multiples ka digital root 9 hota hai (0 nahi), isliye (n-1)%9 + 1 trick use hui hai.

problems.title: Tower of Hanoi: Minimum Moves
problems.problem_statement: n disks on rod A must move to rod C using rod B, one disk at a time, never placing a larger disk on a smaller one. Return the minimum number of moves.
problems.description: Recursive structure samjhna hai: n-1 disks hatao, sabse bada move karo, n-1 wapas upar rakho.
problems.theory: T(n) = 2*T(n-1) + 1 with T(0) = 0, jiska closed form 2^n - 1 hai.

brute_force.approach: Recursion se actual moves simulate/count karo (hanoi(n-1, A, C, B), move, hanoi(n-1, B, A, C)).
brute_force.code_cpp: long long hanoi(int n, char a, char b, char c){ if(n == 0) return 0; long long x = hanoi(n - 1, a, c, b); x += 1; /* move disk n from a to c */ x += hanoi(n - 1, b, a, c); return x; }

optimized.approach: Closed form 2^n - 1.
optimized.code_cpp: long long hanoi(int n){ return (1LL << n) - 1; }

problems.explanation: Sirf count chahiye to moves simulate karne ki zaroorat nahi. Agar actual moves print karne hain to recursion hi chahiye (output khud 2^n - 1 size ka hai).

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.problem_statement: You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. In how many distinct ways can you climb n steps?
problems.description: Order matter karta hai: 1+2 aur 2+1 alag ways hain.
problems.theory: ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2) kyunki last step 1 ya 2 ka ho sakta hai. Ye Fibonacci hi hai.

brute_force.approach: Plain recursion with base cases ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2.
brute_force.code_cpp: int climb(int n){ if(n <= 2) return n; return climb(n - 1) + climb(n - 2); }

optimized.approach: Bottom-up DP, sirf pichhle do values store.
optimized.code_cpp: int climb(int n){ if(n <= 2) return n; int a = 1, b = 2; for(int i = 3; i <= n; i++){ int c = a + b; a = b; b = c; } return b; }

problems.explanation: Brute me ways(3) baar baar compute hota hai. DP me har subproblem ek hi baar solve hota hai. Ye Level 5 DP ka first step hai.

problems.title: Josephus Problem
problems.problem_statement: n people stand in a circle numbered 1..n. Starting from 1, every k-th person is eliminated until one remains. Return the survivor's position.
problems.description: Circle me count continue hota hai aur eliminated person ke baad agle se count dobara 1 se shuru.
problems.theory: Recurrence (0-indexed): J(1) = 0, J(n) = (J(n-1) + k) % n. Answer = J(n) + 1.

brute_force.approach: Vector me saare log rakho aur har baar index = (index + k - 1) % size par erase karo.
brute_force.code_cpp: int josephus(int n, int k){ vector<int> p(n); iota(p.begin(), p.end(), 1); int idx = 0; while(p.size() > 1){ idx = (idx + k - 1) % p.size(); p.erase(p.begin() + idx); } return p[0]; }

optimized.approach: Recurrence ko iterative loop me chalao.
optimized.code_cpp: int josephus(int n, int k){ int r = 0; for(int i = 2; i <= n; i++) r = (r + k) % i; return r + 1; }

problems.explanation: Ek person hatne ke baad problem size n-1 ho jata hai bas positions shift ho jaati hain. Isi shift ko (J(n-1) + k) % n likhte hain.
